age.h2: First things first: what's your age range?
age.hint: This tells us how long your money has to recover from a bad run.
age.label: 60 or over
altChoice.h2: Do you want a small slice in "other investments"?
altChoice.hint: Each one has its own risk threshold — gold gets in at a moderate profile, Bitcoin doesn't. We'll tell you which ones made it.
altChoice.label: Yes, if my profile allows
altKnowledge.h2: Do you know what "other investments" are: crypto, gold, commodities or collectibles?
altKnowledge.label: Yes, I'm clear on that
altLesson.h2: Four families that are neither shares nor bonds
altLesson.trioText: Digital assets with no central bank behind them. The most volatile of the four.
altLesson.trioText2: Gold and friends: the classic safe haven when things turn ugly.
altLesson.trioText3: Oil, wheat, copper. They move with the real economy, not just with interest rates.
altLesson.trioText4: Art, wine, classic cars. No daily market price, so we don't offer them as an option.
altType.hint: Tick as many as you like and set how much each one weighs.
altType.label: Cryptocurrencies
amount.h2: To make it concrete: if you invested today, how much would it be?
amount.h22: And what if you also put in something every month? (optional)
amount.hint: This is only for the examples below, it isn't a real investment.
aria.chart: Historical performance of the recommended portfolio
aria.previewDonut: Live preview of your portfolio breakdown
bondsChoice.h2: What do you want inside your fixed income?
bondsChoice.hint: You can tick several here too, or just take the blended fund if you'd rather not choose.
bondsChoice.label: Government debt
bondsKnowledge.h2: Do you know what fixed income is, and how government debt differs from corporate?
bondsKnowledge.label: Yes, I'm clear on that
bondsLesson.footnote: It's called "fixed" because you know in advance, more or less, how much you get and when. It moves far less than equities and it's what gives the whole portfolio its stability.
bondsLesson.h2: Fixed income is basically lending your money in exchange for interest
bondsLesson.trioText: You lend to the state. The safer of the two.
bondsLesson.trioText2: You lend to big companies. A bit more risk, a bit more interest.
chrome.subtitle: A short illustrated walkthrough to work out which investment portfolio actually makes sense for you — no jargon, real data.
compare.intro: Same period, same data, but concentrating the portfolio into a single asset class.
compare.title: And if you'd put it all into one single thing?
dash.donutHint: Hover over each slice of the doughnut to see what's inside it and how much each part weighs.
dash.eyebrow: With your profile, an illustrative portfolio would look like this
dash.layer2Title: How it would actually have behaved
dash.share: Copy a link to this portfolio
dash.tableFootnote: Rows marked Estimate have no public daily pricing (cash, property crowdfunding and private equity), so they compound at a documented annual rate instead of using market data — which is why they show no real volatility.
equityIndex.h2: What do you want inside your equities?
equityIndex.hint: You can tick several, and set how much each one weighs — watch the doughnut on the right change.
equityIndex.label: S&P 500
equityTilt.h2: Which way do you tilt it?
equityTilt.hint: These go into the same equities block and compete for its weight with what you already picked. Tick what you want and set how much each one weighs.
equityTilt.label: Technology
equityTilt.sublabel3: Defensive: holds up better in crises
equityTiltAsk.h2: Do you also want to tilt your equities towards a specific sector or region?
equityTiltAsk.hint: What you've picked already makes a perfectly good portfolio. This is for anyone who wants, say, more tech, more industry or more Europe than they'd get by default.
equityTiltAsk.label: Yes, let me fine-tune it
footer.p1: This is an educational simulation. It is not financial advice, it executes no real trades, and it should not be the only basis for your investment decisions. Talk to a registered financial adviser before investing real money.
footer.p2: Market data: Twelve Data (free plan). Explanations and lessons generated by Claude (Anthropic) — see the README. Open source on GitHub.
horizon.label: A trip or a near-term goal
indexKnowledge.h2: Do you know the difference between the S&P 500, the NASDAQ 100 and the MSCI World?
indexKnowledge.label: Yes, I know them
indexLesson.h2: Three different baskets of "lots of big companies at once"
indexLesson.trioText: The ~500 biggest US companies. Rides on the US economy.
indexLesson.trioText2: US, heavy on tech. More upside, more scares.
indexLesson.trioText3: Thousands of companies worldwide. The most diversified.
landing.h2: You've never invested and you don't know where to start. That's normal.
landing.note: We don't ask for your email, your account details, or anything you could lose.
landing.p: We'll build an example portfolio for your situation together, with simple illustrated explanations along the way — skippable if you already know your stuff. At the end you'll see how it would actually have behaved.
narrative.intro: The full chain, step by step and with your figures — no black boxes.
narrative.title: Where each percentage comes from
peChoice.h2: Would you like part of it in private equity, if your capital allows?
peChoice.hint: Retail private equity funds usually ask for a higher entry amount than an ETF. We'll tell you if yours falls short, or if your final risk profile doesn't reach it.
peChoice.label: Yes, if my profile and capital allow
peKnowledge.h2: Do you know what private equity is — investing in companies that aren't listed?
peKnowledge.label: Yes, I'm clear on that
peLesson.h2: There are huge giants you simply can't buy on an exchange
peLesson.lessonExamples: Mercadona · El Corte Inglés · Ikea · SpaceX · OpenAI
peLesson.lessonExamples2: ELTIFs aim to lower that minimum
peLesson.trioText: They aren't listed anywhere: there's no way to buy their shares with a click.
peLesson.trioText2: Historically institutional-only, with funds asking for a serious minimum ticket.
peLesson.trioText3: You can't sell whenever you feel like it: it's tied up for years.
preview.title: Your portfolio, live
realEstateChoice.h2: Do you want to put part of it into property?
realEstateChoice.hint: If you say yes, we take a slice off equities and give it to property: your overall risk barely changes.
realEstateChoice.label: Yes, add it
realEstateKnowledge.h2: Did you know you can invest in property without buying a flat?
realEstateKnowledge.label: Yes, I knew that
realEstateLesson.h2: Three ways into property, and only one needs a fortune
realEstateLesson.trioText: A listed company that owns property. You buy a share of it and collect part of the rent as dividends.
realEstateLesson.trioText2: You fund a specific project alongside others. Low entry, but your money is locked in.
realEstateLesson.trioText3: The traditional route. Needs a lot of capital and isn't remotely liquid, so we don't model it here.
realEstateType.hint: You can keep both: the property weight splits between them.
realEstateType.label: REITs
risk.h2: If the money you invested dropped in value overnight, how relaxed would you be?
risk.hint: Put the slider exactly where you want: there are no fixed notches, every point counts.
rvKnowledge.h2: Do you know what equities are, and what an ETF is?
rvKnowledge.label: Yes, I'm clear on that
rvLesson.footnote: Equities are exactly this: nobody promises you what you'll earn. It's the part of a portfolio that rises and falls the most.
rvLesson.h2: From buying one share to buying thousands at once
rvLesson.trioText: A small piece of a company. If Inditex does well, your piece is worth more.
rvLesson.trioText2: Many shares bundled together, so you're not betting everything on one company.
rvLesson.trioText3: A fund that trades on an exchange and tracks a whole index. You buy and sell instantly, and fees are tiny.
style.h2: Would you rather we explain everything in detail, or go straight to the result?
style.label: Explain everything
style.label2: Cut to it, I trust you
volatility.h2: Realistically: how big a drop could you sit through without panic-selling?
volatility.hint: We cross this with your earlier answer: if they don't line up, we lean cautious.
